scope: The exterior of the Cathedral Basilica of the Assumption of Mary in Zacatecas as recorded in late-2000s photographs. Includes the carved three-tier west front, pink cantera bell towers, lower aisles, north and south entrances, octagonal crossing dome and rear chapel. The separately listed parish house, interiors and surrounding urban buildings are outside scope.

references.dateBasis: The native description gives 09/02/2009, interpreted as 9 February for the represented date. The camera EXIF says 30 November 2007. Both indicate the late-2000s state and the exact capture date is uncertain.

originalReview.notes: West-southwest daylight view shows the rose-colored two-stage belfries and patterned caps, the clock on the south tower base, the carved center field, and the cream crossing dome with cantera ribs.
At night the bell chambers read as two distinct levels of paired arched openings. The south side shows the central carved doorway, rougher aisle wall, projecting pilasters and roofline finials.

Daylight side view anchors the south transept entrance, rose ashlar, tower, tall aisle windows, and the octagonal cream dome with its stone ribs. The hand and camera in the foreground are outside scope.

quallaSearch.notes: Started with the exact Qualla original and bound its author’s worldwide public-domain release. Added two exact CC0 exterior views by Álvaro de la Paz Franco from July 2008. Historic images from before completion of the north tower and sources with uncertain rights were excluded.
